headline: Adds a dark mode button to the Recipe Box header that remembers each visitor's choice; small, safe, and fine to ship.
what_changed: A new button in the header next to the search box switches the site between light and dark colours.
The site remembers each visitor's choice on their own device, so it stays the same next time they visit.
First-time visitors get the colour scheme their phone or computer already prefers.
Colour changes now fade in smoothly instead of switching instantly.
All buttons on the site now get a simple outlined style. Right now this is the only button, so nothing else changes.

risks.title: Site could fail to load if browser blocks saved settings
risks.explanation: The app reads and saves the colour choice using the browser's small on-device storage. A few browsers block this storage when the strictest privacy settings are on. For those visitors the page may show up blank instead of just skipping the saved choice. This affects very few people, and a developer can fix it in a few minutes.

risks.title: Search box and page may briefly look wrong in dark mode
risks.explanation: The search box has no dark colours of its own. In dark mode it may stay bright white against the dark page. Visitors who chose dark mode may also see a quick white flash as the page loads. Both are cosmetic and nothing breaks.

questions_for_developer: If a visitor's browser blocks saved settings (some strict privacy modes do), does the site still load? Can we make it fall back to light mode instead?
Can you check the search box and recipe cards in dark mode on a phone and a laptop so everything is easy to read?
good_news: The change is small and touches only appearance. No customer data, payments or accounts are involved.
The saved choice stays only on the visitor's own device and is never sent anywhere.
The button is labelled for screen readers, so visitors with poor or no sight can use it.
